artists.biography:
Blackfield is a collaboratory music project by the English musician Steven Wilson, and Israeli rock singer Aviv Geffen. Together, they have released three albums under the moniker: Blackfield and Blackfield II as equal partners, and Welcome to My DNA with Geffen taking a more dominant role. With the release of Blackfield IV in 2013, Wilson is taking an even more passive role, acting only as a contributor and mixer.

Current band members are drummer Tomer Z, bassist Seffy Efrati, and keyboardist Eran Mitelman. Former band members include Chris Maitland (replaced by Tomer Z, 2004) and Daniel Salomon (replaced by Eran Mitelman, 2007).

Collaborative era:
Formed after a meeting in 2000, the partnership blossomed into a cross-cultural collaboration called Blackfield.

Aviv had discovered Porcupine Tree in the mid ‘90s and followed their career development. In 2000 he invited the band to perform some concerts in Israel and met with Steven in London to discuss working together. Before long they had collaborated on the first Blackfield song. In 2001 the two met in a studio in Tel Aviv with the intention of recording a one-off EP.

The results of the session were so impressive however, that the EP was cancelled and the decision was made to continue writing and recording a full length album. Over the next 18 months the pair fitted in Blackfield writing and recording sessions whenever they could between their other commitments and finally in October 2003 the debut album was complete.

The collaborative songs alongside songs written by each separately brought a unique meeting of cultures, which resulted in the self titled album, which was hailed at the time as ‘hypnotically effective’ (Classic Rock) and ‘another strike of genius from Steven Wilson’ (Eclipsed).

perplexity.description:
For The Music," released in 2020, is a studio album by Blackfield, a collaborative project blending rock, pop, and progressive rock elements. The album continues the band's established style of melodic, artful songwriting, combining atmospheric textures with accessible rock and pop sensibilities. It reflects the artistic partnership between Israeli musician Aviv Geffen and English songwriter Steven Wilson, though this release emphasizes a more streamlined, song-focused approach compared to some of their earlier, more progressive works.

Positioned as a mature entry in Blackfield's discography, "For The Music" follows their tradition of crafting emotionally resonant and polished tracks that balance introspective lyrics with rich instrumentation. Released under Warner Music Central Europe, the album received positive attention for its cohesive sound and strong songwriting, appealing both to longtime fans and new listeners within the progressive and alternative rock scenes. While not a commercial blockbuster, it was well-regarded critically for maintaining the band's signature blend of melodic rock and thoughtful production.
